sanskrit: tad ajñānān mahat pāpaṃ kṛtvā saṃkulitendriyaḥ ekas tv acintayaṃ buddhyā kathaṃ nu sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: Having committed that great sin through ignorance, with senses distraught, I pondered alone in my mind: how could any good come of this?

sanskrit: tatas taṃ ghaṭam ādaya pūrṇaṃ paramavāriṇā āśramaṃ tam ahaṃ prāpya yathākhyātapathaṃ gataḥ
english: Then, taking up that pot filled with the finest water, I reached the hermitage by the path that had been described to me.

sanskrit: tatrāhaṃ durbalāv andhau vṛddhāv apariṇāyakau apaśyaṃ tasya pitarau lūnapakṣāv iva dvijau
english: There I saw his parents — blind, frail, aged, bereft of a guide, like two birds with clipped wings.

sanskrit: tannimittābhir āsīnau kathābhir aparikramau tām āśāṃ matkṛte hīnāv udāsīnāv anāthavat
english: Seated, unable to move about, conversing on matters concerning him, they were deprived of that hope I should have brought, sitting helpless like the unprotected.

sanskrit: padaśabdaṃ tu me śrutvā munir vākyam abhāṣata kiṃ cirāyasi me putra pānīyaṃ kṣipram ānaya
english: Upon hearing the sound of my footsteps, the sage spoke these words: "Why do you delay, my son? Bring the water quickly."

sanskrit: yannimittam idaṃ tāta salile krīḍitaṃ tvayā utkaṇṭhitā te māteyaṃ praviśa kṣipram āśramam
english: "On account of what, dear child, were you sporting in the water so long? Your mother here has been anxious — enter the hermitage quickly."

sanskrit: yad vyalīkaṃ kṛtaṃ putra mātrā te yadi vā mayā na tan manasi kartavyaṃ tvayā tāta tapasvinā
english: "Whatever offence your mother or I may have given you, dear son, an ascetic such as you ought not to take it to heart."

sanskrit: tvaṃ gatis tv agatīnāṃ ca cakṣus tvaṃ hīnacakṣuṣām samāsaktās tvayi prāṇāḥ kiṃ cin nau nābhibhāṣase
english: "You are the refuge of the refugeless, the eyes of those without sight — our very lives cling to you. Why do you not speak even a word to us?"

sanskrit: munim avyaktayā vācā tam ahaṃ sajjamānayā hīnavyañjanayā prekṣya bhīto bhīta ivābruvam
english: Frightened, like one truly stricken with fear, I looked upon that sage and spoke to him in a voice that faltered, unclear, and almost without sound.

sanskrit: manasaḥ karma ceṣṭābhir abhisaṃstabhya vāgbalam ācacakṣe tv ahaṃ tasmai putravyasanajaṃ bhayam
english: Steadying the strength of speech with effort of mind and body, I disclosed to him the dread calamity born of the destruction of his son.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo 'haṃ daśaratho nāhaṃ putro mahātmanaḥ sajjanāvamataṃ duḥkham idaṃ prāptaṃ svakarmajam
english: "I am Daśaratha the kṣatriya — I am not the son of the great soul. This grief, scorned by good men, has come upon me through my own deed."

sanskrit: bhagavaṃś cāpahasto 'haṃ sarayūtīram āgataḥ jighāṃsuḥ śvāpadaṃ kiṃ cin nipāne vāgataṃ gajam
english: "Reverend one, I came to the bank of the Sarayū, bow in hand, seeking to kill some beast of prey or an elephant that had come to the watering-place."

sanskrit: tatra śruto mayā śabdo jale kumbhasya pūryataḥ dvipo 'yam iti matvā hi bāṇenābhihato mayā
english: "There I heard a sound of a pot being filled with water; taking it for an elephant, I struck with an arrow."

sanskrit: gatvā nadyās tatas tīram apaśyam iṣuṇā hṛdi vinirbhinnaṃ gataprāṇaṃ śayānaṃ bhuvi tāpasaṃ
english: "Going then to the river's bank, I saw an ascetic lying on the ground, his heart pierced by the arrow, life departed."

sanskrit: bhagavañ śabdam ālakṣya mayā gajajighāṃsunā visṛṣṭo 'mbhasi nārācas tena te nihataḥ sutaḥ
english: "Venerable one, having detected that sound while I was seeking to slay an elephant, I released an iron-tipped arrow into the water — by that your son has been slain."

sanskrit: sa coddhṛtena bāṇena tatraiva svargam āsthitaḥ bhagavantāv ubhau śocann andhāv iti vilapya ca
english: "He, with the arrow drawn out, attained heaven right there, lamenting and weeping over you both, the blind ones."

sanskrit: ajñānād bhavataḥ putraḥ sahasābhihato mayā śeṣam evaṃgate yat syāt tat prasīdatu me muniḥ
english: "Your son was struck by me suddenly, through ignorance. Whatever must follow given what has occurred — may the sage be gracious to me."

sanskrit: sa tac chrutvā vacaḥ krūraṃ niḥśvasañ śokakarśitaḥ mām uvāca mahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalim upasthitam
english: Upon hearing those cruel words, heavily sighing, emaciated by grief, that great and radiant sage spoke to me as I stood before him with folded hands.

sanskrit: yady etad aśubhaṃ karma na sma me kathayeḥ svayam phalen mūrdhā sma te rājan sadyaḥ śatasahasradhā
english: "Had you not yourself confessed this inauspicious deed to me, O king, your head would have instantly shattered into a hundred thousand fragments."

sanskrit: kṣatriyeṇa vadho rājan vānaprasthe viśeṣataḥ jñānapūrvaṃ kṛtaḥ sthānāc cyāvayed api vajriṇam
english: "A killing committed by a kṣatriya knowingly and deliberately, especially of a forest-dweller, would unseat even the wielder of the thunderbolt from his station."

sanskrit: ajñānād dhi kṛtaṃ yasmād idaṃ tenaiva jīvasi api hy adya kulaṃ nasyād rāghavāṇāṃ kuto bhavān
english: "Because this was done through ignorance, you live by that very reason alone. Otherwise the entire Rāghava lineage might perish this very day — how much more you yourself."

sanskrit: naya nau nṛpa taṃ deśam iti māṃ cābhyabhāṣata adya taṃ draṣṭum icchāvaḥ putraṃ paścimadarśanam
english: "Lead us to that place, O king" — thus he also addressed me: "We wish today to see our son for a last sight."

sanskrit: rudhireṇāvasitāṅgaṃ prakīrṇājinavāsasaṃ śayānaṃ bhuvi niḥsaṃjñaṃ dharmarājavaśaṃ gatam
english: His limbs smeared with blood, his bark garment scattered, lying on the ground without consciousness, passed into the power of the king of righteousness.

sanskrit: athāham ekas taṃ deśaṃ nītvā tau bhṛśaduḥkhitau asparśayam ahaṃ putraṃ taṃ muniṃ saha bhāryayā
english: Then I alone, leading those two who were deeply stricken with grief to that place, caused that sage — together with his wife — to touch their son.

sanskrit: tau putram ātmanaḥ spṛṣṭvā tam āsādya tapasvinau nipetatuḥ śarīre 'sya pitā cāsyedam abravīt
english: Having touched and approached their son, those two ascetics fell upon his body, and his father spoke these words over him:

sanskrit: na nv ahaṃ te priyaḥ putra mātaraṃ paśya dhārmika kiṃ nu nāliṅgase putra sukumāra vaco vada
english: "Am I then not dear to you, my son? Look upon your mother, O righteous one. Why do you not embrace me, dear tender child? Speak a word."

sanskrit: kasya vāpararātre 'haṃ śroṣyāmi hṛdayaṃgamam adhīyānasya madhuraṃ śāstraṃ vānyad viśeṣataḥ
english: "From whom in the latter part of the night shall I hear the sweet, heart-stirring sound of recitation of scripture, or any other discourse especially dear to me?"

sanskrit: ko māṃ saṃdhyām upāsyaiva snātvā hutahutāśanaḥ ślāghayiṣyaty upāsīnaḥ putraśokabhayārditam
english: "Who, having worshipped at twilight, bathed, and offered into the sacred fire, will praise and sit attending upon me, tormented as I am by grief and fear for a son?"

sanskrit: kandamūlaphalaṃ hṛtvā ko māṃ priyam ivātithim bhojayiṣyaty akarmaṇyam apragraham anāyakam
english: "Who will bring tubers, roots, and fruit and feed me as a beloved guest — helpless, unprotected, without a guide?"

sanskrit: imām andhāṃ ca vṛddhāṃ ca mātaraṃ te tapasvinīm kathaṃ putra bhariṣyāmi kṛpaṇāṃ putragardhinīm
english: "How, my son, shall I maintain this wretched mother of yours — blind, aged, an ascetic woman, pitifully longing for a son?"

sanskrit: tiṣṭha mā mā gamaḥ putra yamasya sadanaṃ prati śvo mayā saha gantāsi jananyā ca samedhitaḥ
english: "Stay, do not go, my son, toward the abode of Yama. Tomorrow you shall go together with me, accompanied by your mother as well."

sanskrit: ubhāv api ca śokārtāv anāthau kṛpaṇau vane kṣipram eva gamiṣyāvas tvayā hīnau yamakṣayam
english: "Both of us too, stricken with grief, helpless and wretched in the forest, bereft of you, shall very quickly go to the realm of Yama."

sanskrit: tato vaivasvataṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ pravakṣyāmi bhāratīm kṣamatāṃ dharmarājo me bibhṛyāt pitarāv ayam
english: "Then, upon seeing Vaivasvata, I shall speak this plea: 'May the king of righteousness pardon me; let him sustain these parents of mine.'"

sanskrit: apāpo 'si yathā putra nihataḥ pāpakarmaṇā tena satyena gacchāśu ye lokāḥ śastrayodhinām
english: "Just as you, my son, though slain by the deed of a sinner, are yourself without sin — by that truth, go swiftly to the worlds of those who fight with weapons."

sanskrit: yānti śūrā gatiṃ yāṃ ca saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinaḥ hatās tv abhimukhāḥ putra gatiṃ tāṃ paramāṃ vraja
english: "The supreme goal attained by heroes who do not retreat in battles, slain while facing the enemy — to that supreme goal, my son, do you proceed."

sanskrit: yāṃ gatiṃ sagaraḥ śaibyo dilīpo janamejayaḥ nahuṣo dhundhumāraś ca prāptās tāṃ gaccha putraka
english: "The goal attained by Sagara, Śaibya, Dilīpa, Janamejaya, Nahuṣa, and Dhundhumāra — to that goal go, dear child."

sanskrit: yā gatiḥ sarvasādhūnāṃ svādhyāyāt patasaś ca yā bhūmidasyāhitāgneś ca ekapatnīvratasya ca
english: "The goal of all virtuous ones, and the goal of one who has fallen from his own Vedic study, of a giver of land, of one who has kindled sacred fires, of one who has kept the vow of a single wife —"

sanskrit: gosahasrapradātṝṇāṃ yā yā gurubhṛtām api dehanyāsakṛtāṃ yā ca tāṃ gatiṃ gaccha putraka na hi tv asmin kule jāto gacchaty akuśalāṃ gatim
english: "— the goal of givers of a thousand cows, the goal of those who have served their teachers, and the goal of those who have surrendered their bodies — to that goal go, dear child. For no one born in this lineage goes to an ill-fated destination."

sanskrit: evaṃ sa kṛpaṇaṃ tatra paryadevayatāsakṛt tato 'smai kartum udakaṃ pravṛttaḥ saha bhāryayā
english: Thus he lamented miserably there over and over again; then he proceeded, together with his wife, to perform the water-offering for him.

sanskrit: sa tu divyena rūpeṇa muniputraḥ svakarmabhiḥ āśvāsya ca muhūrtaṃ tu pitarau vākyam abravīt
english: But the sage's son, by virtue of his own deeds, having taken on a divine form, consoled his parents for a moment and then spoke these words:

sanskrit: sthānam asmi mahat prāpto bhavatoḥ paricāraṇāt bhavantāv api ca kṣipraṃ mama mūlam upaiṣyataḥ
english: "Through service to you both I have attained a great station. You two shall also swiftly come to me at my abode."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu divyena vimānena vapuṣmatā āruroha divaṃ kṣipraṃ muniputro jitendriyaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the sage's son — his senses mastered — quickly ascended to heaven in a radiant divine chariot.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā tūdakaṃ tūrṇaṃ tāpasaḥ saha bhāryayā mām uvāca mahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalim upasthitam
english: That ascetic of great radiance, having quickly performed the water-offering together with his wife, spoke to me as I stood before him with folded hands.

sanskrit: adyaiva jahi māṃ rājan maraṇe nāsti me vyathā yac chareṇaikaputraṃ māṃ tvam akārṣīr aputrakam
english: "Slay me today, O king — I feel no anguish at death. For by your arrow you have made me, who had but one son, sonless."

sanskrit: tvayā tu yad avijñānān nihato me sutaḥ śuciḥ tena tvām abhiśapsyāmi suduḥkham atidāruṇam
english: "But because my pure son was slain by you through ignorance, by that I shall curse you with an exceedingly terrible and dreadful sorrow."

sanskrit: putravyasanajaṃ duḥkhaṃ yad etan mama sāmpratam evaṃ tvaṃ putraśokena rājan kālaṃ kariṣyasi
english: "Just as this grief born of the loss of a son is now mine, so too, O king, shall you meet your end through grief for a son."

sanskrit: tasmān mām āgataṃ bhadre tasyodārasya tad vacaḥ yad ahaṃ putraśokena saṃtyakṣyāmy adya jīvitam
english: Therefore, O auspicious one, that is the noble utterance which has come upon me — that today I am abandoning my life through grief for a son.

sanskrit: yadi māṃ saṃspṛśed rāmaḥ sakṛd adyālabheta vā na tan me sadṛśaṃ devi yan mayā rāghave kṛtam
english: "If Rāma were to touch me even once today, or embrace me even once, it would not equal what I have done to the Rāghava, O queen."

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā tvāṃ na paśyāmi smṛtir mama vilupyate dūtā vaivasvatasyaite kausalye tvarayanti mām
english: "I cannot see you with my eyes; my memory is failing. These messengers of Vaivasvata, O Kausalyā, are pressing me to hasten."

sanskrit: atas tu kiṃ duḥkhataraṃ yad ahaṃ jīvitakṣaye na hi paśyāmi dharmajñaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākyamam
english: "What grief could be greater than this — that at the extinguishing of my life I cannot see Rāma, the knower of righteousness, the refuge of truth?"

sanskrit: na te manuṣyā devās te ye cāruśubhakuṇḍalam mukhaṃ drakṣyanti rāmasya varṣe pañcadaśe punaḥ
english: "Those who will behold Rāma's face adorned with beautiful auspicious earrings again in the fifteenth year — they are not mere mortals but gods."

sanskrit: padmapatrekṣaṇaṃ subhru sudaṃṣṭraṃ cārunāsikam dhanyā drakṣyanti rāmasya tārādhipanibhaṃ mukham
english: "Blessed are they who will behold Rāma's face — lotus-petal-eyed, fair-browed, with beautiful teeth and lovely nose — resembling the lord of stars."

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ śāradasyendoḥ phullasya kamalasya ca sugandhi mama nāthasya dhanyā drakṣyanti tanmukham
english: "Blessed are they who shall see the face of my lord — like the autumn moon, like a bloomed lotus, fragrant."

sanskrit: nivṛttavanavāsaṃ tam ayodhyāṃ punar āgatam drakṣyanti sukhino rāmaṃ śukraṃ mārgagataṃ yathā
english: "Happy are they who shall see Rāma returned from forest-dwelling, come back to Ayodhyā — like the planet Śukra traversing its path."

sanskrit: ayam ātmabhavaḥ śoko mām anātham acetanam saṃsādayati vegena yathā kūlaṃ nadīrayaḥ
english: "This grief born of my own self assails me — helpless, unconscious — with force, as a river's current assails its bank."

sanskrit: hā rāghava mahābāho hā mamāyāsa nāśana rājā daśarathaḥ śocañ jīvitāntam upāgamat
english: "Ah, Rāghava of mighty arms! Ah, destroyer of my afflictions!" — grieving thus, King Daśaratha reached the end of his life.

sanskrit: tathā tu dīnaṃ kathayan narādhipaḥ priyasya putrasya vivāsanāturaḥ gate 'rdharātre bhṛśaduḥkhapīḍitas tadā jahau prāṇam udāradarśanaḥ
english: Thus narrating in misery, the lord of men — anguished by the banishment of his beloved son, tormented by overwhelming grief — when midnight had passed, that noble-visaged king gave up his life.

sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prātar evāpare 'hani bandinaḥ paryupātiṣṭhaṃs tat pārthivaniveśanam
english: Then, when the night had passed and the next day's morning came, the bards presented themselves around the royal dwelling.

sanskrit: tataḥ śucisamācārāḥ paryupasthāna kovidaḥ strīvarṣavarabhūyiṣṭhā upatasthur yathāpuram
english: Then those skilled in courtly attendance, pure in conduct — a group consisting mostly of women of the finest quality — presented themselves as was customary.

sanskrit: haricandanasaṃpṛktam udakaṃ kāñcanair ghaṭaiḥ āninyuḥ snānaśikṣājñā yathākālaṃ yathāvidhi
english: Those versed in the lore of bathing brought water mixed with yellow sandal in golden pots at the proper time and in the proper manner.

sanskrit: maṅgalālambhanīyāni prāśanīyān upaskarān upaninyus tathāpy anyāḥ kumārī bahulāḥ striyaḥ
english: Other women — many of them young maidens — also brought the auspicious implements to be touched and the articles to be tasted.

sanskrit: atha yāḥ kosalendrasya śayanaṃ pratyanantarāḥ tāḥ striyas tu samāgamya bhartāraṃ pratyabodhayan
english: Then those women who attended most closely upon the bedchamber of the lord of Kośala came together and tried to awaken their husband.

sanskrit: tā vepathuparītāś ca rājñaḥ prāṇeṣu śaṅkitāḥ pratisrotas tṛṇāgrāṇāṃ sadṛśaṃ saṃcakampire
english: Seized with trembling and anxious for the life of the king, they trembled like the tips of grass in a current against the stream.

sanskrit: atha saṃvepamanānāṃ strīṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam yat tad āśaṅkitaṃ pāpaṃ tasya jajñe viniścayaḥ
english: Then, seeing the trembling women and the king, that which had been dreaded as evil became a certainty.

sanskrit: tataḥ pracukruśur dīnāḥ sasvaraṃ tā varāṅganāḥ kareṇava ivāraṇye sthānapracyutayūthapāḥ
english: Then those noble women cried out aloud in distress, like female elephants in the forest whose herd-leader has strayed from his place.

sanskrit: tāsām ākranda śabdena sahasodgatacetane kausalyā ca sumitrāca tyaktanidre babhūvatuḥ
english: Kausalyā and Sumitrā, their consciousness suddenly roused by the sound of their wailing, abandoned sleep.

sanskrit: kausalyā ca sumitrā ca dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca pārthivam hā nātheti parikruśya petatur dharaṇītale
english: Kausalyā and Sumitrā, seeing and touching the king, cried out "Ah, my lord!" and fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: sā kosalendraduhitā veṣṭamānā mahītale na babhrāja rajodhvastā tāreva gaganacyutā
english: She, the daughter of the lord of Kośala, writhing upon the earth, covered with dust, shone not — like a star fallen from the sky.

sanskrit: tat samuttrastasaṃbhrāntaṃ paryutsukajanākulam sarvatas tumulākrandaṃ paritāpārtabāndhavam
english: That scene — with people in panic and confusion, thronged with anxious crowds, tumultuous lamentation on all sides, and kinsmen stricken with anguish —

sanskrit: sadyo nipatitānandaṃ dīnaviklavadarśanam babhūva naradevasya sadma diṣṭāntam īyuṣaḥ
english: — with joy instantly extinguished, with a sight of misery and distress, became the royal dwelling of the king who had gone to his fated end.

sanskrit: atītam ājñāya tu pārthivarṣabhaṃ yaśasvinaṃ saṃparivārya patnayaḥ bhṛśaṃ rudantyaḥ karuṇaṃ suduḥkhitāḥ pragṛhya bāhū vyalapann anāthavat
english: Knowing that the most illustrious bull among kings had departed, his wives surrounded him and — weeping bitterly, overcome with deep sorrow, raising their arms — lamented pitifully, like the unprotected.

sanskrit: tam agnim iva saṃśāntam ambuhīnam ivārṇavam hataprabham ivādityaṃ svargathaṃ prekṣya bhūmipam
english: Beholding the king who had gone to heaven — like a fire extinguished, like an ocean drained of water, like the sun robbed of its radiance —

sanskrit: kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇākṣī vividhaṃ śokakarśitā upagṛhya śiro rājñaḥ kaikeyīṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: — Kausalyā, her eyes full of tears, emaciated by grief in many ways, clasping the head of the king, addressed Kaikeyī:

sanskrit: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi bhuṅkṣva rājyam akaṇṭakam tyaktvā rājānam ekāgrā nṛśaṃse duṣṭacāriṇi
english: "Your wish is fulfilled, Kaikeyī — enjoy the kingdom free of thorns. Having abandoned the king, O cruel woman, O woman of wicked conduct, be single-minded now."

sanskrit: vihāya māṃ gato rāmo bhartā ca svargato mama vipathe sārthahīneva nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "Rāma has gone, abandoning me; my husband has gone to heaven. Like a traveller stranded on a wrong road without companions, I have no wish to live."

sanskrit: bhartāraṃ taṃ parityajya kā strī daivatam ātmanaḥ icchej jīvitum anyatra kaikeyyās tyaktadharmaṇaḥ
english: "Abandoning that husband as her deity — what woman would wish to live otherwise? Only Kaikeyī, she who has abandoned righteousness."

sanskrit: na lubdho budhyate doṣān kiṃ pākam iva bhakṣayan kubjānimittaṃ kaikeyyā rāghavāṇān kulaṃ hatam
english: "The greedy one perceives no fault — as if consuming something cooked; for the sake of a hunchback, Kaikeyī has destroyed the lineage of the Rāghavas."

sanskrit: aniyoge niyuktena rājñā rāmaṃ vivāsitam sabhāryaṃ janakaḥ śrutvā paritapsyaty ahaṃ yathā
english: "Rāma together with his wife was exiled by the king who was engaged in what was not his proper duty. Janaka, upon hearing this, will grieve as deeply as I do."

sanskrit: rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣo jīvanāśam ito gataḥ videharājasya sutā tahā sītā tapasvinī duḥkhasyānucitā duḥkhaṃ vane paryudvijiṣyati
english: "Rāma of lotus-petal eyes has gone from here to the destruction of his comfortable life. And Sītā — that afflicted daughter of Videha's king, unaccustomed to sorrow — will tremble with anguish in the forest."

sanskrit: nadatāṃ bhīmaghoṣāṇāṃ niśāsu mṛgapakṣiṇām niśamya nūnaṃ saṃstrastā rāghavaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati
english: "Hearing in the nights the fearsome roars of beasts and birds, surely terrified, she will cling to Rāghava."

sanskrit: vṛddhaś caivālpaputraś ca vaidehīm anicintayan so 'pi śokasamāviṣṭo nanu tyakṣyati jīvitam
english: "Old and with few children, not thinking of Vaidehī, he too — seized by grief — will surely abandon his life."

sanskrit: tāṃ tataḥ saṃpariṣvajya vilapantīṃ tapasvinīm vyapaninyuḥ suduḥkhārtāṃ kausalyāṃ vyāvahārikāḥ
english: Then, embracing that afflicted woman as she lamented, the attendants led away Kausalyā who was overwhelmed with deep grief.

sanskrit: tailadroṇyām athāmātyāḥ saṃveśya jagatīpatim rājñaḥ sarvāṇy athādiṣṭāś cakruḥ karmāṇy anantaram
english: Then the ministers, having laid the lord of the earth in a vat of oil, were instructed and immediately performed all the rites for the king.

sanskrit: na tu saṃkalanaṃ rājño vinā putreṇa mantriṇaḥ sarvajñāḥ kartum īṣus te tato rakṣanti bhūmipam
english: However, the all-knowing ministers did not dare to perform the king's cremation without his son; therefore they preserved the king's body.

sanskrit: tailadroṇyāṃ tu sacivaiḥ śāyitaṃ taṃ narādhipam hā mṛto 'yam iti jñātvā striyas tāḥ paryadevayan
english: Knowing that that lord of men had been laid by the ministers in the vat of oil — "Ah, he is dead!" — those women lamented.

sanskrit: bāhūn udyamya kṛpaṇā netraprasravaṇair mukhaiḥ rudantyaḥ śokasaṃtaptāḥ kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayan
english: Raising their arms in misery, with faces streaming from their eyes, weeping, scorched by grief, they lamented pitifully.

sanskrit: niśānakṣatrahīneva strīva bhartṛvivarjitā purī nārājatāyodhyā hīnā rājñā mahātmanā
english: Like a night bereft of stars, like a woman bereft of her husband, the city of Ayodhyā did not shine, deprived of the great-souled king.

sanskrit: bāṣpaparyākulajanā hāhābhūtakulāṅganā śūnyacatvaraveśmāntā na babhrāja yathāpuram
english: With people overwhelmed with tears, with the women of noble families crying "Alas! Alas!", with empty crossroads and house-interiors, it shone not as before.

sanskrit: gataprabhā dyaur iva bhāskaraṃ vinā vyapetanakṣatragaṇeva śarvarī purī babhāse rahitā mahātmanā na cāsrakaṇṭhākulamārgacatvarā
english: Like a sky that has lost its radiance without the sun, like a night from which the company of stars has departed, the city bereft of the great-souled king had no splendour — nor did its roads and crossroads throng with voices choked with tears.

sanskrit: narāś ca nāryaś ca sametya saṃghaśo vigarhamāṇā bharatasya mātaram tadā nagaryāṃ naradevasya saṃkṣaye babhūvur ārtā na ca śarma lebhire
english: Men and women, coming together in groups and reviling the mother of Bharata, were stricken with anguish at the destruction of their king, and found no comfort in that city.
